newsitem.title: USA: Oct cash flows to US stock funds about $13 bln - ICI.
newsitem.headline: Oct cash flows to US stock funds about $13 bln - ICI.

text.p: New cash flows into U.S. stock mutual funds dropped to $13 billion in October, according to a preliminary estimate by an industry trade group, continuing a trend of slower growth that began in May.
The estimated $13 billion that went into stock funds compared with a $17.4 billion net inflow in September, said the Investment Company Institute, a mutual fund trade group.
The evidence suggests the slowdown was concentrated among domestic funds, said John Rea, the group's chief economist.
Bond and income funds had modest cash outflows in October for the fourth time in six months, the group said. The outflow was $0.5 billion, compared with an inflow of $1.93 million in September.
Rea said the October outflow happened despite a decline in long-term interest rates that had brought positive returns for many bond funds.
Overall, long-term mutual funds of all types saw inflows of $12.5 billion in October, compared with actual inflows of $19.36 billion in September.
